title: Recipe 18 — Multi-Provider Fallback (breakers, cascade, and the declarative path first)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 18 is availability, not cost or quality routing. And it opens by telling you to reach for the spec fields first — so that is where this drive starts too.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipes and starters are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env. A live two-provider hop needs Anthropic and OpenAI credentials both.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the declarative path — model_fallbacks and circuit_breaker

beats.label: Type the spec-level failover block
beats.cue: “Since 0.2.0 fallback is a spec field. An ordered candidate list, and breaker tuning whose field names mirror the package exactly — this is recipe 59's committed spec, which recipe 18 sends you to first.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean. model_fallbacks and circuit_breaker are first-class spec surface, not annotations the compiler tolerates.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “There they are, lowered: modelFallbacks as an ordered array, circuitBreaker with the three thresholds. Sugar in the YAML, data in the IR.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli — agent.modelFallbacks + agent.circuitBreaker present

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, no key. The only thing missing is a credential the spec itself declares.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Find the chain in the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Two generated lines — the candidate array and the breaker options — wired into the loop. The compiled runtime does the cascade; you did not write it.”

beats.label: Resolve five model strings
beats.cue: “The router parses the prefix and lazy-loads only the matching adapter. A Claude-primary spec never imports the OpenAI SDK — cold start scales with what you actually use.”
beats.command: bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { parseModelString } from "@crewhaus/model-router"; for (const m of ["claude-sonnet-5", "openai/gpt-4o", "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash", "bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0", "groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile"]) { const p = parseModelString(m); console.log(p.providerId.padEnd(10), p.modelId); }'

verify.note: anthropic / openai / gemini / bedrock / openai — the recipe's grammar table, resolved from live/dist/node_modules with no credentials. groq lands on the openai-compatible adapter, which is why GROQ_API_KEY never collides with OPENAI_API_KEY

groups.title: Beat 3 · the machinery underneath — the hand-wired cascade

beats.label: Type the recipe's cascade loop
beats.cue: “When you need per-call control the spec blocks do not expose — a custom isFailure, different tuning per candidate, your own ordering — this is the whole thing. Resolve, wrap, cascade.”

beats.label: Open what we just wrote
beats.cue: “One breaker per candidate, kept in a map — so a bad Anthropic trips the Anthropic breaker and leaves OpenAI healthy. And note it cascades at turn granularity, never mid-stream.”

beats.label: Prove it is real TypeScript
beats.cue: “Transpiled, and the two imports it needs named back at us. The recipe's building blocks are two packages — nothing else.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const src = require("fs").readFileSync("live/fallback.ts", "utf8"); const t = new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: "ts" }); t.transformSync(src); console.log("fallback.ts: valid TypeScript —", t.scanImports(src).map((i) => i.path).join(" + "))'

groups.title: Beat 4 · trip a breaker on camera

beats.label: Three failures against a threshold of three
beats.cue: “A stub adapter that always throws, wrapped with failureThreshold 3. Three failed streams and the state goes open — from here calls fail fast with no network touched, and the cascade falls through to the next candidate.”
beats.command: bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { wrap } from "@crewhaus/circuit-breaker"; const stub = { providerId: "anthropic", features: {}, estimateTokens: () => 1, async *stream() { throw new Error("simulated upstream 503"); } }; const b = wrap(stub, { adapterName: "claude-sonnet-5", failureThreshold: 3 }); for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { try { for await (const _ of b.stream({ model: "x", system: [], messages: [], maxTokens: 8 })) {} } catch {} } console.log("claude-sonnet-5 after 3 failures → state:", b.state(), "| stats:", JSON.stringify(b.stats()))'

verify.note: state: open · stats {state:open, consecutiveFailures:0, transitions:1, lastTrippedAt:…} — the real @crewhaus/circuit-breaker out of the bundle --check installed, no credentials involved

beats.label: Launch the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Now the chain is live: Anthropic primary, GPT-4o second, Groq third. Healthy, every turn goes to the primary.”

verify.note: interactive REPL; a real cascade needs credentials for at least two providers

beats.label: Ask it something
beats.cue: [needs-key] With CREWHAUS_TRACE=pretty on, a breaker transition would render in red right here.
beats.text: In one sentence: what does a circuit breaker protect a caller from?

groups.title: One more thing · the whole state machine, asserted

beats.label: Run the recipe's Try-it smoke
beats.cue: “Probe 3 is recipe 18's own end-to-end: five injected failures trip the breaker, the cooldown elapses, a probe succeeds, and it closes. Three transitions on the bus, in order.”

verify.note: all probes passed — probe 3 asserts closed→open→half_open→closed and exactly 3 circuit_state_changed events. Redirected rather than piped so the exit code is the smoke's own

beats.label: Read the probe log
beats.cue: “That is the recovery profile from the recipe's timeline: trip, cooldown, half-open probe, closed. Per process, in memory, each worker probing independently.”
